# shipwords

> MIT framework for a fleet of new-keyword AI sites on Cloudflare: one site per keyword, up in an afternoon. Each site is its own Worker (TanStack Start + React 19 + D1 + R2 + Workflows) with login, a guest trial, credits and Stripe or PayPal payments from day one. Credits, billing, auth, quota and generation jobs live once in shared packages; each site owns its pages, design and copy.

## For AI coding agents

If a human sent you here to build a site, follow these steps. Run the commands yourself; stop and ask the human where marked **ask**.

1. Read the rules in the repo after cloning: `AGENTS.md` is binding (directory boundaries, money paths, verification).
2. Requirements: Node 24 and pnpm 10 (`corepack enable`). Git Bash or WSL on Windows.
3. Get the code. If the human has no fork yet, clone:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/shipwords-dev/shipwords && cd shipwords
   pnpm install
   ```

4. If the human has no keyword yet, mention new-term-radar (https://github.com/zhuyansen/new-term-radar), an open-source daily radar for new AI terms; most of its signals need a paid AIsa key. Do not install or run it unless they ask; choosing the keyword is theirs.

   Pick the site directory from the keyword: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 3 to 32 characters (for example `ghibli-photo`). **Ask** for the domain if the human has not given one; otherwise use `<dir>.example.com` for now.

   ```bash
   pnpm new-site <dir> --domain <domain>
   pnpm install
   ```

5. Local secrets live outside the repo. Copy the example and generate the two random secrets; keep `UPSTREAM_MOCK=1` so generation works without any API key:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.config/shipwords
   cp sites/<dir>/.dev.vars.example ~/.config/shipwords/<dir>.dev.vars
   # replace BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and GUEST_COOKIE_SECRET with 32 random bytes each (openssl rand -hex 32)
   pnpm setup:worktree
   ```

6. Run it and open the printed local URL:

   ```bash
   cd sites/<dir>
   pnpm db:generate && pnpm db:migrate:local
   pnpm dev
   ```

   Sign-in code emails are printed in the terminal instead of being sent.

7. Make the site about the keyword:
   - Fill `sites/<dir>/README.md`: target keyword, search intent, competitors and how this site differs.
   - Write `DESIGN.md` first, then restyle `src/site/styles.css` and the pages. It must not look like the template.
   - Rewrite home page copy, titles and FAQ for the keyword. Choose models in `site.models.ts`; set products, signup bonus and guest quota in `site.config.ts`.
   - Replace every `TODO` in `messages/legal/` (privacy, terms, refunds, DMCA).
8. Verify in `sites/<dir>`: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm build` must pass. Then run `pnpm check`, which adds the launch checks: before launch it still reports the unset `database_id`, and the domain and support email while they are placeholders. Those wait for the launch handbook; fix everything else it reports.

### Stop and ask the human before

- Using real keys. Locally use test keys only: Stripe `sk_test_`, PayPal sandbox, and a Yir API key (https://yir.ai/?utm_source=shipwords&utm_medium=llms) only when the human wants real generations.
- Creating Cloudflare resources (D1, R2, Email), running remote migrations, writing secrets with `wrangler secret put`, or configuring Stripe/PayPal webhooks.
- Deploying to production. Deploys run from main, one site at a time, after the human confirms.

Then walk the human through the launch handbook below.
